_doc: The numbers and names prep.py runs on: how it batches, retries and times out the Source2Viewer-CLI (VRF) exports from the player's CS2 VPK, and where it looks for weapon stats items_game.txt does not give. Read from prep/prep.json (a copy of this sheet) on the player's PC. The rows are this build's choices; vdata_keys maps CS2 weapon vdata fields to the items_game attribute names Weapons.gd reads, every one unverified until a real CS2 weapons.vdata has been read.

rows.used_by: prep_cs2.export: most VPK paths in one VRF -f call
rows.note: fewer calls means less VRF start-up time (it opens the 30+ GB VPK index each run)

rows.used_by: prep_cs2.export: longest comma-joined -f list in one VRF call
rows.note: Windows CreateProcess caps a command line at 32767 characters; this keeps a call far under it with long install paths
rows.verified: build choice; the 32767 limit is the documented Windows CreateProcess limit

rows.used_by: prep_cs2.export: after the batched calls, each file that still failed the output check is exported again on its own this many times
rows.note: one file per call on a retry, so one bad path cannot cost the rest of its batch
rows.verified: build choice; tested with a fake VRF that drops files (prep/tests/test_export.py)

rows.used_by: prep_cs2.run_vrf: a VRF call that runs longer is killed and its files count as failed (then retried)
rows.note: the 0.1.0 install exported 5 models and clips in one call well inside this; 40 weapon models per call is unmeasured
rows.verified: build choice, unverified against a real 40-model call

rows.used_by: prep_cs2.cs2_step: exported on its own after items_game.txt; read by prep/kv3.py for any stat items_game.txt does not give
rows.note: optional: a VPK without it is not a problem by itself, only weapons left without the stats in stats_required are
rows.verified: unverified: path from memory of CS2 modding notes, not seen in a VPK listing here

rows.used_by: prep_cs2.write_stats: a weapon without every one of these (from items_game.txt or weapons.vdata) stops setup, so no install runs its guns on weapon_defaults.json class averages
rows.note: the other attributes fall back to weapon_defaults.json and are listed as a warning in prep_status.json
rows.verified: build choice; tested in prep/tests/test_prep.py (missing damage blocks the done file)

rows.value: primary clip size,spread,inaccuracy fire,recoil magnitude,max player speed
rows.used_by: prep_cs2.write_stats: a weapon missing any of these still finishes setup, with a warning in prep_status.json naming it (those values come from weapon_defaults.json class averages)
rows.note: every gun has these in CS:GO's items_game.txt; zoom and alt keys are left out because only some guns have them
rows.verified: build choice; the CS:GO key names are from its items_game.txt, the CS2 file is unverified here
